name: ai-rerank
summary: Reorder search results by relevance to a query
description: Cross-encoder style reranking over candidates the caller already holds. Fuses the platform's six per-aspect embedding scores (visual/colour/texture/style/material/understanding) into one ordering using claude-haiku-4-5. Degrades to the SOURCE ORDER on every failure path - fewer than 2 candidates, no API key, model error, or a model reply naming ids that were not sent - and reports which happened in `reranked`/`reason`, so a caller never mistakes an unranked list for a ranked one. Ranks by id rather than index, so a shifted candidate list cannot silently reorder the wrong results. The same logic runs in-process for the agent's material_search, visual_search and knowledge_base_search tools; this endpoint is for callers outside the agent runtime. Prompt is editable at /admin/ai-configs (prompts.category='ai_rerank').

Driven nightly at 03:40 by the facets-recanonicalize-degraded cron with degraded_only=true; a full catalog re-sweep costs a Voyage embedding per raw value and must be requested explicitly. Requires service-role or x-cron-secret (isCronAuthorized) — an open proxy here would be an open Voyage spend. Returns `remaining` so the caller knows whether to run again.

degraded.description: Still failing; deliberately NOT version-bumped so they stay eligible and are retried first

remaining.description: Products still below target_version. -1 means the count itself failed — explicitly unknown, never a comforting 0.

description: Requires Supabase JWT. Routes on body.action to execute-flow (run a saved flow with trigger data), test-flow (dry-run, no side effects), or trigger-event (auto-dispatch from DB triggers or server-to-server).

params.name: flow_id
params.desc: UUID of the flow to execute.

params.name: trigger_data
params.desc: Arbitrary payload passed as trigger context into the graph.

actions.response: {success: boolean, data: {id: string, status: string, results: object}}

actions.name: test-flow
actions.summary: Dry-run a flow: resolves templates and evaluates conditions but does not fire actions.

params.name: flow_id
params.desc: UUID of the flow to test.

actions.response: {success: boolean, data: {id: string, status: string, results: object}}

actions.name: trigger-event
actions.summary: Auto-dispatch flows whose trigger_type matches the event type; used by DB triggers and internal services.

params.name: event_data
params.desc: Event payload merged into trigger context.

request.name: action
request.desc: One of: execute-flow | test-flow | trigger-event

name: flow-scheduler-cron
summary: Per-minute cron that fires scheduled flows whose cron expression matches current UTC time.
description: Validates x-cron-secret, fetches active flows with trigger_type='scheduled', evaluates their cron expression against the current time (with timezone support), and invokes flow-engine execute-flow for each due flow. Prevents double-firing with a 55-second last_run_at guard.
response: {success: boolean, checked: number, triggered: number, results: array}

name: flow-webhook
summary: Receives external HTTP requests and routes them to the matching webhook-triggered flow.
description: Requires flow_id as a query parameter. Validates that the flow has trigger_type='webhook' and is active. Optionally verifies an X-Webhook-Secret header against the secret stored in the flow's trigger_config before delegating to flow-engine execute-flow.

request.desc: UUID of the webhook-triggered flow to execute.

response: {success: boolean, data: {flow_id: string, run_id: string, status: string}}

name: gsc-api
summary: Google Search Console for connected websites (OAuth + performance sync)
description: Connects a user_website to a Google Search Console property and pulls first-party search-analytics (query/page/clicks/impressions/ctr/position) into gsc_performance. OAuth is SERVER-SIDE: Google's redirect_uri points at THIS function (GET ?code&state); it exchanges the code and 302s back to /profile?tab=websites&gsc=<connected|pick_property|error>. This avoids the SPA's supabase-js (detectSessionInUrl+PKCE) intercepting Google's ?code= as a login code. `state` is an HMAC-signed {website_id,user_id,ts} minted at authorize-time after authenticate()+userCanAccessWorkspace(). Tokens live in website_gsc_connections (service-role only). verify_jwt disabled so the GET callback + cron (x-cron-secret, action=cron-sync) work.

name: viva-webhooks
summary: Viva.com payment webhook receiver + verification-key handshake (multi-tenant BYOK)
description:
#273 Phase 2 - Viva.com webhooks, multi-tenant BYOK. Two surfaces:

- GET  - the verification-key handshake Viva performs at webhook registration. The key is per-merchant, so the caller passes ?workspace_id=<uuid> to say which tenant is registering; the function fetches that workspace's key from Viva and echoes it back.
- POST - the event deliveries: 1796 payment created, 1797 reversal created, 1798 payment failed, 2054 account transaction (merchant-level, covers incoming RF bank transfers).

SECURITY: Viva payment webhooks carry NO per-message signature (Viva-Signature-256 exists only on their Data Services contract, which has a shared secret; payment webhooks have none), so there is nothing to verify per delivery. Invariant #6 is satisfied differently and more strongly: THE WEBHOOK IS A TRIGGER, NEVER DATA - the handler reads the transaction back from Viva's API and acts on that, so a forged delivery cannot inject state. Settled 1796/RF payments are mirrored into the unified bank feed (provider viva, informational).

name: real-estate-public
summary: Anonymous, token-gated public listing pages, buyer portal, discovery and lead capture
description:
The unauthenticated half of Real Estate — deliberately a separate function from `real-estate-api` so no authed surface is reachable without a session. Uses the service-role client, but every read is bound to an opaque capability token (`public_listing_token` / buyer `portal_token`); there is no id-addressable public read. Only listings that are `is_public` **and** `listing_status='active'` resolve — anything else 404s.

Responses are the `toPublic()` projection only: internal pricing, owner and lead fields never leave. Lead-writing actions require `gdpr_consent`, derive property + workspace from the token (never the body), and are throttled to **8 submissions per hour per IP** (IP is SHA-256 hashed, never stored raw) → 429.

description:
PULL syndication: a portal fetches `GET /real-estate-feed?token=…&format=kyero|openimmo|generic` and receives the workspace's live listings as XML. The opaque `feed_token` (rotatable from `real-estate-api → rotate-feed-token`) is the only credential — it gates cross-workspace enumeration.

A listing only appears when it is `is_public`, `listing_status='active'` **and** `in_discovery=true`, so a listing published only to the agency's own site never leaks to third-party portals. Output is the `toPublic()` projection with XML-escaped values. `format` falls back to the workspace's configured `feed_format`. A disabled or unknown token returns a 404 XML error document.

name: real-estate-buyer-digests
summary: Daily cron — emails saved-search digests to buyers with a matching new listing
description: For every active buyer requirement with `digest_enabled`, a `portal_token` and a contact email, finds listings that match the saved criteria **and** were published since `last_digest_at`, then emails a summary linking to `/buyer/:token`. Stamps `last_digest_at` so the same listing never re-sends. A buyer with nothing new is skipped silently (no empty email). Runs daily via pg_cron; auth is the shared cron gate (`x-cron-secret` **or** service-role bearer).

name: real-estate-calendar
summary: Pushes viewings into the agent's own Google Calendar (per-user OAuth)
description: Viewings already sync to the platform calendar (`crm_meetings`); what an agent lives in is Google Calendar on their phone, and a viewing they cannot see there is one they miss. Reuses the platform GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and the token/refresh shape already proven in `gsc-api`, so Google is configured once rather than once per feature. Actions: `status`, `connect` (returns the consent URL), `disconnect`, `push-viewing`. The GET path is Google's OAuth callback. The connection is per USER and its RLS is owner-only — it holds one person's tokens and workspace membership deliberately grants nothing. `state` is HMAC-signed with the service key and carries user + workspace, so the callback cannot be replayed to bind someone else's Google account; `prompt=consent` forces a refresh_token even on reconnect, without which a stored connection dies within the hour. `push-viewing` re-checks the caller may see the viewing before writing to any calendar, cancels the Google event when the viewing is cancelled, and records `last_sync_error` rather than swallowing it — a calendar that silently stops syncing looks exactly like one with no viewings.
response: { connected, google_email, last_sync_at, last_sync_error, configured } | { auth_url } | { ok, event_id }

name: real-estate-ical
summary: Short-let channel sync — availability feed out (GET, token) and channel calendars in (POST, cron)
description: Booking channels all speak iCalendar and nothing else, so this one function is the whole integration. **GET ?token=…** serves the availability feed a channel pulls, authorised solely by the per-listing `ical_token`; it publishes BLOCKED NIGHTS ONLY — no guest name, email or price — because that URL is a bearer capability handed to third parties. **POST** (shared cron gate) pulls every active `property_channel_links.ical_import_url`, re-validating each through the shared SSRF guard at read time as well as write time, and upserts on `(property, channel, UID)` so a channel republishing its whole calendar every poll does not duplicate every stay. A `23P01` exclusion violation on import is reported as a date conflict rather than swallowed — that IS a double booking, and only the operator can resolve it on the channel that sold it twice. Runs hourly.
response: text/calendar (GET) | { ok, links, imported, conflicts, failed } (POST)

name: real-estate-inbound-lead
summary: Public tokenised endpoint — turns a forwarded portal enquiry email into a CRM lead
description: Syndication pushes listings out; the enquiries portals generate come back as email. An agency points any inbound-email service (Resend, Mailgun routes, SendGrid Inbound Parse, Cloudflare Email Workers) at this URL and forwards portal mail to it. The per-workspace `inbound_lead_token` IS the credential and is checked BEFORE anything is parsed or written — the From address is spoofable and is used only to guess which portal sent it. Fails closed: unknown token or ingestion disabled both return the same 401, so probing cannot confirm a valid token. `workspace_id` comes from the token and `property_id` from the listing's own `reference_code`; nothing identifying is taken from the payload. Parses name / email / phone / reference / message, skipping the portal's own no-reply address, routes the lead through `route_property_lead`, and keeps the parsed source in `inbound_raw` because portal formats change silently. A message with no contactable details returns 200 (a digest or receipt must not be retried forever).
response: { ok, inquiry_id, portal, matched_listing, assigned } | { ok, skipped }

name: real-estate-listing-social
summary: Flow action — drafts a social post for a newly published listing, one per connected account
description: Invoked by the seeded `realestate.listing_published` flow via `run_edge_function`. Builds a caption from the listing's own fields (no AI, no credits — an unreviewed generated caption on a property ad is where fair-housing language goes wrong), signs the cover photo out of the private `property-media` bucket, and inserts a **draft** `social_posts` row per active connected account. Deliberately stops at draft: `zernio-api` authorises publishing against a real workspace member, and this runs service-role from a flow with no user — publishing here would mean weakening the check that stops one tenant posting through another tenant's account. Idempotent (an existing post carrying the same `metadata.property_id` short-circuits) and skips listings that are not publicly live. Auth is the shared cron gate (`x-cron-secret` **or** service-role bearer).
response: { ok, posts, drafted_for, has_image } | { ok, skipped }

name: real-estate-vendor-reports
summary: Weekly cron — emails the instructing vendor a performance report on their own listing
description: For every `active` listing with `vendor_reports_enabled` and a vendor contact carrying an email, builds the vendor report (views/enquiries/viewings and days-on-market from `get_property_performance`, recent completed-viewing feedback, and a comps-based price recommendation from the agency's own stock) and emails it. A service communication under the agency agreement rather than marketing, so it is gated per listing on `vendor_reports_enabled` — not on `crm_contacts.marketing_consent`. Stamps `last_vendor_report_at` only on a successful send, so a failed week retries instead of being skipped, and re-sends no sooner than 6 days. Runs weekly (Mondays 07:00 UTC) via pg_cron; auth is the shared cron gate (`x-cron-secret` **or** service-role bearer).

name: real-estate-rent-invoicing
summary: Daily cron — drafts Finance invoices for rent charges coming due
description: For every `due`/`overdue` rent charge on an active tenancy with a tenant, falling due within the next **7 days** and not yet invoiced, creates a **DRAFT** Finance invoice to the tenant and links it back on the charge (`property_rent_charges.invoice_id`). Drafts are deliberately never transmitted to myDATA — the property manager reviews VAT and document type and issues them from Finance. Batched at 500 charges per run. Requires the `real-estate-management` add-on to have produced the rent schedule in the first place.

name: crm-lead-score
summary: AI lead + health scoring for any CRM contact (canonical platform scorer)
description:
Scores **any** `crm_contacts` lead from generic CRM signals (activity recency, engagement, company fit, pipeline position), enriched with property signals when the Real Estate module is enabled. Writes the shared `crm_contacts.lead_score` (0-100, likelihood to transact soon) and `health_score` (0-100, engagement/fit) so CRM, Sales and Real Estate all render the SAME number rather than three private scores.

Not module-gated — lead scoring is a CRM-wide capability. Uses Anthropic tool-use (`emit_lead_score`) so the verdict is schema-locked, never a parsed blob. Credit-metered reserve→settle at a 3-credit ceiling, with an automatic refund when the model returns no usable output.

name: monitoring-cron
summary: Unified monitoring dispatcher — one function behind all five price / mention / job cron tasks
description:
Replaces the five near-identical monitoring crons (`price-monitoring-cron`, `mention-monitoring-cron`, `llm-mention-probe-cron`, `job-research-cron`, `job-research-digest-cron`). Each was the same boilerplate — cron-secret check → module gate → POST to a MIVAA cron endpoint — differing only in module slug and path.

pg_cron passes `?task=<task>`. The task gates on its own module toggle (a disabled module returns `{skipped:'module_disabled'}` rather than running a paid refresh) and then delegates to MIVAA, which selects the due rows and processes them in batch. Auth is the shared cron gate: `x-cron-secret` **or** a service-role bearer, so a vault/env secret-name drift can no longer 401 all five tasks at once.

External API consumers (`api_key_id IS NOT NULL`) are intentionally never touched by the refresh tasks — they pay per call and control their own cadence.

query.desc: Which monitoring sweep to dispatch. Unknown values return 400 with the known list.

response: { success, task, ...MIVAA result } | { success:true, task, skipped:"module_disabled" } | { error }

name: moodboard-dormancy-cron
summary: Daily cron — notify-then-delete lifecycle for idle moodboards
description:
Storage-retention sweep for moodboards. A board idle for 30 days gets a **warning** email + bell notification carrying a one-click keep-active link; a reminder follows as the grace window closes; only then is the board removed. Nothing is deleted without the owner having been told first, twice.

The keep-active link resolves through the public `moodboard-keep-active` function. Backed by the `moodboard_dormancy_scan` RPC. Note that moodboards are **user**-scoped, not workspace-scoped, so notification targeting is per-owner.

name: moodboard-keep-active
summary: Public one-click "keep this moodboard" target for the dormancy warning email
description:
GET `/moodboard-keep-active?token=<keep_active_token>`. Validates the token, clears the pending dormancy schedule and bumps `updated_at` so the activity clock resets, then renders a small self-contained HTML confirmation page.

Public by design (`verify_jwt = false`) so the link works straight from an email client with no login. The 96-hex-character random token **is** the capability; an invalid or already-consumed token renders the failure page rather than revealing whether the board exists.

query.desc: keep_active_token from the dormancy email link.

name: taric-reference-sync
summary: Import the EU TARIC goods nomenclature (Greek extract) into the reference table
description: Loads a CSV/TSV export of the TARIC goods nomenclature into public.taric_codes, which backs the commodity-code picker, code validation and the classifier shortlist. Column headers are matched against an alias table so the EU export, the Greek national export and an admin re-export all load unconfigured. Admin JWT for the import; the monthly refresh cron authenticates with x-cron-secret and fetches TARIC_REFERENCE_URL.

Row counts and last-import timestamp for the reference table.

name: taric-classify
summary: Propose a TARIC commodity code for catalog products
description: Three stages, cheapest first: a supplier-declared HS/CN/TARIC code found in the product attributes is validated and applied directly; otherwise search_taric_codes shortlists candidates and Claude picks one through a forced tool call. The model result is NEVER written to products.taric_code — it lands in taric_code_suggested with a confidence for a human to confirm, because a tariff misclassification is a customs liability. Stage C debits one credit per product before the upstream call; the hourly backfill cron runs with llm=false so it only applies free supplier-declared codes.

Cron only. Sweeps products at taric_status=pending for supplier-declared codes. Body: mode=backfill, limit, llm=false.

name: revolut-api
summary: Revolut Business connection management (per-workspace BYOK) — keys, OAuth, accounts, mapping, sync
description: #315. Actions on one POST surface: init (mint RSA keypair server-side; private key never leaves the server), authorize-url (Revolut consent URL), oauth-complete (exchange the auth code via JWT client assertion), register-webhook (webhooks v2 subscription + signing secret), accounts (live Revolut accounts + finance_bank_accounts mapping), map-account (link a Revolut currency pocket to a bank account row), sync-now (shared sync core for this workspace), disconnect. Caller must be a finance manager of the target workspace (RLS-checked; 404 on mismatch) and the workspace must be entitled to banking-revolut (402 otherwise). validate-account-name proxies Revolut CoP/VoP so the CRM bank area can confirm an IBAN belongs to the named counterparty; map-account auto-fills the finance row IBAN/BIC from /accounts/{id}/bank-details when empty. Phase 2 adds reconciliation: reconcile re-runs the invoice matcher; confirm-match settles a statement line against an invoice through record-payment; ignore-transaction parks a line. Phase 3 adds money-out: create-counterparty mirrors a CRM bank row as a Revolut counterparty (VoP-gated; not_matched blocks unless force=true); send-payment creates a draft (human approves in-app) or a direct transfer; create-payout-link pays without an IBAN; fx-rate/exchange convert between pockets. Every instruction is audited in revolut_payouts with an idempotent request_id before Revolut is called. Phase 4 adds team cards (issue virtual, freeze/unfreeze) and card-expense browsing with on-demand receipt passthrough (never persisted). import-expenses attributes card expenses to employees (card→holder email→HR roster) into monthly expense reports with receipts; also runs with the cron sweep, which additionally freezes cards of offboarded employees. pay-due-bills drafts ONE multi-payment run over due supplier_bills (suppliers without a VoP-linked counterparty are skipped and reported); set-card-limit patches weekly/monthly spending caps; create-card-invitation invites a new member by email. sync-labels pushes platform finance categories into a "Platform categories" Revolut label group (names only, never deletes). reconcile also settles OUTGOING transfers against supplier_bills (reference-quotes-bill-number or exact-amount+supplier-name; payments direction out + payment_allocations.supplier_bill_id). confirm-bill-match manually settles an OUTGOING revolut feed line against a supplier bill. The feed table is now multi-provider (revolut|stripe|viva); stripe/viva rows are informational mirrors of webhook-settled money and are guarded against re-matching.

name: revolut-sync
summary: Revolut transaction sync sweep — cron backstop over every connected workspace
description: #315. Pulls transactions since each workspace's watermark (first run: 365 days) and upserts statement lines into revolut_bank_transactions, deduped on workspace + '<txid>:<legid>'. Dual auth like finance-inbound-sync: x-cron-secret/service-role for the cron path; a JWT user path restricted to the caller's own workspaces. Skips workspaces whose banking-revolut entitlement lapsed. Failures land in workspace_revolut_config.last_sync_error (explicit failure marker, never a silent zero). The sweep also pulls Stripe balance transactions (Connect workspaces) into the unified feed as informational rows.

name: revolut-webhooks
summary: Revolut Business webhooks v2 receiver — signed transaction events, per-workspace secret
description: #315. Registered per workspace with ?ws=<workspace_id>; the config row's webhook_signing_secret verifies each delivery (HMAC-SHA256 over v1.<timestamp>.<body>, 5-minute replay window, timing-safe compare). Fail-closed: no stored secret → 503, bad signature/stale timestamp → 400, unknown ws → bland 200 so workspace ids cannot be enumerated. TransactionCreated upserts statement lines into revolut_bank_transactions (silver layer); TransactionStateChanged updates state. Reconciliation into payments is a separate explicit step — the webhook never writes money tables. Also handles PayoutLinkCreated/StateChanged to keep the revolut_payouts audit state live.

request.desc: Workspace whose signing secret verifies this delivery.

name: revolut-merchant-webhooks
summary: Revolut Merchant (checkout) webhook receiver + per-workspace webhook setup
description: #315 payments-revolut. Two surfaces: POST ?setup=1 (user JWT, finance manager, module entitlement) registers the merchant webhook with the tenant's own secret key and stores the signing secret; POST ?ws=<workspace_id> receives signed deliveries (HMAC v1.<timestamp>.<body>, 5-min window, fail-closed 503 without a stored secret). On ORDER_COMPLETED the order is re-read from the Merchant API with the tenant's key (webhook-as-trigger doctrine) and settled through record-payment; intent status paid, duplicate-safe, cross-tenant guarded.

name: workspace-webhooks-api
summary: Manage a workspace's outbound webhook endpoints
description: Tenant-facing CRUD for outbound webhook subscriptions (#330). Actions: list, create, update, rotate_secret, delete, deliveries. The HMAC signing secret is generated server-side and returned exactly once (on create and rotate_secret) - the column is revoked from the authenticated role and cannot be read back. Endpoint URLs are https-only and pass the shared SSRF guard before they are stored. Event types are validated against SUBSCRIBABLE_EVENT_TYPES. workspace_id is always reconciled against the caller's JWT; an endpoint belonging to another workspace returns 404, not 403.

name: workspace-webhook-dispatcher
summary: Deliver queued outbound webhook events to tenant endpoints
description: Cron function that POSTs queued deliveries to tenant endpoints (#330). Signs each request HMAC-SHA256 over '{timestamp}.{body}' and sends it as X-MaterialKai-Signature, with the timestamp inside the signed string so a captured delivery cannot be replayed later. Re-runs the shared SSRF guard at delivery time (not just at registration - DNS behind a stored hostname can be re-pointed) and refuses to follow redirects. Retries with exponential backoff to a hard attempt cap; an SSRF rejection fails immediately rather than retrying. An endpoint that fails enough consecutive deliveries is auto-disabled.

name: page-watch-webhook

Firecrawl does NOT sign its webhooks, so authentication is a shared secret sent in the `x-firecrawl-webhook-secret` header, set on the monitor at creation time and compared in constant time. Fails closed with 503 when FIRECRAWL_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset. The tenant is resolved from `page_watches` by `firecrawl_monitor_id` — never from the payload. Replays are absorbed by a unique index on (page_watch_id, firecrawl_check_id, url).

name: page-watches
summary: CRUD for watched pages, mirrored to Firecrawl monitors.
description: Action-dispatched endpoint backing the Page Monitoring UI. Creates, updates and deletes a Firecrawl monitor alongside each `page_watches` row so the two never drift — a row deleted without its monitor would keep billing on its schedule. Requires a user JWT; the supplied workspace_id is verified against the caller's membership before any read or write. `run` debits a Firecrawl credit before starting the check and refuses with 402 if the debit fails. Gated on the `page-monitoring` module.

goal.description: Natural-language definition of a meaningful change; enables Firecrawl's judge

is_active.description: update only; pauses the upstream monitor too

name: customer-assets-api
summary: Installed base: a customer's equipment, its warranties and its recurring service schedules (#343).
description: Action-discriminated JWT endpoint over customer_assets, customer_asset_warranties, customer_asset_service_plans and customer_asset_service_events, plus the per-product defaults in product_service_defaults. Reads and writes run through the caller's own RLS context; registration and service completion go through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that call assert_workspace_member. There is no next_due_on field anywhere: the next due date IS the plan's single open service event, served by the customer_asset_service_due view. Ownership mismatches return 404, never 403. Warranty certificates upload through this function (service-role write to the private pdf-documents bucket under warranties/, after ownership is proven on the RLS-bound client) and are read via a short-lived signed URL; the row stores bucket + path and never a URL. Deleting an asset that has logged service returns 409 - the DB refuses it so the history cannot be erased.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace; verified against the caller's memberships.

asset_id.description: Equipment id, for the asset-scoped actions.

event_id.description: Service occurrence id, for service.complete / service.skip.

response: { assets } | { asset, warranties, plans, events } | { asset_id } | { due } | { history } | { next_event_id } | { defaults } | { warranty } | { url } | { success }

name: asset-service-reminders-cron
summary: Cron: emit equipment service-due, service-overdue and warranty-expiring flow events (#343).
description: Runs daily via pg_cron (x-cron-secret via isCronAuthorized). Scans the customer_asset_service_due view for open occurrences inside their lead-time window and customer_asset_warranties approaching ends_on, then emits asset.service_due, asset.service_overdue and asset.warranty_expiring flow events with the recipient resolved from the plan assignee, the customer's responsible sales users, or the workspace owners/admins. It never writes a user_notifications row or calls email-api directly — the seeded system-default flows deliver. Each reminder is stamped on its row so it fires once, and only after the emit actually succeeded; a transient failure leaves the row unstamped for the next tick. Backed by the ops.asset_reminders_silent_zero integrity probe.
response: { success, scanned_due, scanned_warranties, serviceDue, serviceOverdue, warrantyExpiring, failed }
